reason: A ratio (length or height as a multiple of diameter). It is a measurement, not a structure, like the earlier rejected 'times width' and 'times calyx'.
A length ratio against the leaves ('1-2 times leaves'). It is a comparison, not a structure, like 'times calyx'.
A length-to-diameter ratio. A measurement, not a structure.
A ratio against the length of a tube, and the tube is not named. A measurement, not a structure.
A general part that needs the organ it belongs to ('projection' was rejected on 2026-11-13). 'Toothlike' is a shape, not a separate structure.
Narrower use. Floras mean the non-reproductive shoot: stems and leaves that are glabrescent or fetid-smelling. The roots are seldom meant.
'apiculum' and 'apiculus' were rejected on 2026-11-13 as general parts that need their organ. 'with' is part of the presence phrase, not of the name.
Exact. 'leaf blade' is a synonym of leaf lamina, and 'sheaths with blades' says the lamina is present on sheathing leaves (sedges, grasses). 'with' belongs to the presence phrase.
Narrower. 'hair' is a synonym of trichome. 'Acicular' (needle-shaped) is a shape quality to annotate separately, not a new class.
Exact. 'adventitious root' is a listed synonym of shoot-borne root, and 'nodes with adventitious roots' is the classic case.
Different families use 'antennae' for unrelated appendages (orchid column or flower appendages, other floral or fruit processes). It is ambiguous without the organ.
Close to exact. Pollen sac lists 'anther lobe' as a synonym. Floras sometimes say 'anther sacs' for the thecae (one theca holds two pollen sacs), so the match is a little loose.
A general part ('appendage' was rejected on 2026-11-13). 'Apical' gives a position but not the organ.
The teeth could belong to a calyx, leaf, capsule, bract or lemma. A general part that needs its organ, like the rejected 'terminal lobe'.
Exact. A broken singular of 'apices' (plural of apex). It maps like the unqualified 'apex' rule C266. The count ('apices 2') is a count of apices on the part being described.
A general part ('appendage' was rejected). 'Basal' gives a position but not the organ.
Narrower. Plural of 'basal vein', which the 2026-11-13 review (C272) already mapped to leaf lamina vein.
PO has no bract vein class. Vein = vascular bundle (as for 'nervure', C273), expressed as a part of the bract with the part-of-whole pattern.
Narrower. A leafy bract. Bract already covers 'hypsophyll'.
A fragment that includes the quality 'present'. 'callus' was rejected on 2026-11-13 as a general part (orchid lip, lemma). PO 'plant callus' is a different thing (wound or tissue-culture tissue).

Narrower. These are sheathing leaves, often bladeless, on the stem (orchids, sedges). 'Cauline' is the position quality FLOPO:0991117. If they are only bladeless cataphylls, scale leaf (PO_0006003) is the other choice.
A general part ('cavity' was rejected on 2026-11-13). 'Surface with dense cavities' is better read as a pitted surface quality of the named part.
A measurement used as the second term of a ratio (hilum length as a share of the seed's circumference). Not a structure.
Narrower. A compound cyme with umbel-like branching. 'Umbellate' and 'compound' are qualities of the cyme, so no new class is needed.
A broken singular of the adjective 'contiguous' ('contiguous pairs'), a relational quality. 'contiguous' was rejected on 2026-11-13.
A general part ('groove' was rejected). Dorsal grooves of mericarps, seeds, achenes and fruits differ, so the organ is needed.
A shape quality ('renflements ellipsoïdes' = ellipsoid swellings). The noun was cut off.
Exact. 'Walls thick' would ideally go on the cell wall, but the cell class is the right bearer for this name.
Exact. Another wording of 'epidermal cell'.
An adverb that qualifies a quality ('fairly narrow', 'fairly well-differentiated'). It is a fragment, not a structure.
